answer: Every new agent must queue at a registration jetty that issues only a few berths each epoch, a hard bottleneck. Before docking, the applicant keeps a small ember of slashable stake alight through several live challenge rounds. Graders then compare the newcomer against a velvet map of behavioral fibers—timing, phrasing, neighbor overlap—and matches collapse clones into one berth and slash. An attacker who wants many votes must wait in that queue and fund a separate deposit per identity, so mass forgeries stall at the dock instead of flooding the vote.
